VisualCardPool.rationale: `=> ModelDb.CardPool<DefectCardPool>()` (RipAndTear.cs:18) selects the card's ART pool. Presentation.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Event, TargetType.RandomEnemy)` (RipAndTear.cs:20-23) == cost 1 / ATTACK / EVENT / RANDOM_ENEMY. The RANDOM_ENEMY target type is what keeps the framework from resolving a single target up front (combat.py:463-468 only resolves ANY_ENEMY), leaving the per-hit roll to the card.

CanonicalVars.rationale: `new DamageVar(7m, ValueProp.Move)` (RipAndTear.cs:16) == `_damage = 7`; the hit count of 2 is a literal `WithHitCount(2)` in C# (27) rather than a RepeatVar, and the sim stores it as `_hits = 2` so `base_hits` reports it -- the same small improvement card/maul makes.

OnPlay.rationale: Closed 2026-07-27: the per-hit target roll now runs on the named stream. `trash_heap_cards.py:288-296` takes `crng = ctx.combat.combat_rng` and, when `crng.is_parity`, picks with `crng.targets.choice(living)` -- `targets` maps to `combat_targets` (combat_rng.py:22,52) -- keeping the shared `random.Random` only on the legacy RL arm, which is the two-branch shape card/sword_boomerang already used and this entry named as the fix. VERIFIED AGAINST THE SOURCE, NOT THE COMMENT: src/Core/Commands/Builders/AttackCommand.cs:601-602 reads `Rng combatTargets = (Attacker.Player ?? Attacker.PetOwner).RunState.Rng.CombatTargets; singleTarget = combatTargets.NextItem(validTargets);` -- one draw on CombatTargets per hit, inside the per-hit loop, which is exactly one `crng.targets.choice` per iteration of `for _ in range(self._hits)`. The halves that were already faithful are unchanged: the per-hit re-derivation of `living` from `is_gone`, the duplicates-allowed policy, and the break when no target remains. Legacy mode is byte-identical to before, because `CombatRng.legacy` hands every accessor the same `random.Random` the else-arm uses (combat_rng.py:37-39, wired at combat.py:94-97). HISTORY -- WHAT THE DIVERGENCE WAS: The per-hit re-roll, the duplicate policy and the living-target filter are all faithful. C#'s `TargetingRandomOpponents(CombatState)` defaults `allowDuplicates: true` (AttackCommand.cs:309, 325) and `_doesRandomTargetingAllowDuplicates` is initialised true (72), so both hits MAY land on the same enemy -- which the sim's independent `choice` per hit reproduces -- and AttackCommand re-derives `validTargets` from `where c.IsAlive` at the top of each hit (544-546) == the sim's per-hit `[e for e in ctx.combat.enemies if not e.is_gone]`, with both breaking when none remain. WRONG RNG STREAM: C# rolls `(Attacker.Player ?? Attacker.PetOwner).RunState.Rng.CombatTargets.NextItem(validTargets)` (AttackCommand.cs:601-602); the sim calls `ctx.combat._rng.choice(living)` (trash_heap_cards.py:288) on the unseeded shared `random.Random`, even though `ctx.combat.combat_rng.targets` maps to `combat_targets` (combat_rng.py:22,54) and `CombatState.auto_play_card` already uses it correctly with the CardCmd.cs:77 citation in-line (combat.py:540-546). LIVE -- Rip and Tear is a ported Event Attack from the Trash Heap, the targets parity stream is wired, and under a string-seeded run the two hits land on different enemies than the recorded run. Same mechanism and same verdict as the other shared-rng cards (rule 3); this is the 10th of the 21 the probe lists. Presentation, folded in: the NScratchVfx hit node. REGRESSION TEST: `test/test_rng_tripwire.py:33` (`test_no_wrong_stream_draws_in_random_run`, 20 seeded full runs) is the standing gate for this whole family. It wraps `RunState.rng` and asserts ZERO in-combat draws on it; `CombatState` receives that same object as `self._rng` (run.py:1146-1148, combat.py:88), so a `ctx.combat._rng` draw taken from inside a card's `on_play` is recorded and fails the gate -- verified by playing this family's shape under a `Tripwire` and getting a hit at the `card.on_play` frame (combat.py:490). The gate is green today, so these 20 seeds never reach this card's draw; routing the site to the named `combat_rng` accessor is verified by keeping it green.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `DynamicVars.Damage.UpgradeValueBy(2m)` (RipAndTear.cs:35) == `self._damage += 2` (7 -> 9). The hit count stays 2 when upgraded on both sides.
